newsitem.title: USA: SEC failure to supervise cases rising - official.
newsitem.headline: SEC failure to supervise cases rising - official.

text.p: The SEC has said it will bring more actions against securities firm officials for failing to supervise employees, and it is delivering on that warning, SEC General Counsel Richard Walker said Friday.
"This issue has never been as high a concern at the Securities and Exchange Commission," Walker said at a Public Securities Association conference here.
Walker said the SEC brought seven "failure to supervise" cases in 1991, 24 in 1993, 13 in 1994 and 25 in 1995. He said the total could exceed 25 in 1996.

Walker said that self-regulatory organizations also are bringing more failure to supervise cases. The New York Stock Exchange, for instance, brought 10 to 12 such cases in the 1990s compared to almost none in the 1980s, Walker said.
SEC also is looking at stiffer sanctions in this area, Walker said. SEC not only will suspend or bar an official from serving as a supervisor, but it may seek a "time out" TOO.

"In some cases there will be some coupling where someone will be barred industry wide for a period of time and then have a supervisory bar, which will continue for some period after that," Walker said.
